title: Rabbi Chalafta of Hevah – of Huna (of Haifa)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Gittin 86b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.86b.14) Rabbi Yochanan said to the sons of Rabbi Chalafta of Huna (another version: Haifa): “Thus said your father: She need never leave [her husband], and a tick in a column does not disqualify the water of purification.” This statement is cited in [Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot, chapter 3, beginning of halakhah 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.3.9.3), and [Gittin, chapter 9, beginning of halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.9.3.3), where Rabbi Yochanan transmits it in the name of Rabbi Chalafta of Hevah.

notes.text: The supplied column expression differs from the named witness’s sheaf reading. The letter/word question is retained rather than converted into a claim that the physical source has been verified. The notice remains held for that expression.

The linked Yevamot reads Hevah, while the corresponding passage in Jerusalem Talmud Gittin spells the place חוח. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1329&lang=en) records Huna and Haifa in the Bavli tradition and discusses the Yerushalmi form.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. II, p. 454) reads קרצית שבעמיר, “a kartzit in the sheaf,” as does the consulted Gittin 86b. The supplied transcription reads קרצית שבעמוד, “a tick in a column,” and is retained in the translation. Abaye describes the kartzit as a fly found among sheaves. The second ruling concerns purification water. The first concerns leaving the second husband after remarriage on the basis of a defective bill of divorce. The Jerusalem Talmud parallels concern the first ruling. The consulted Hebrew reads הוה in Yevamot 3:9 and חוח in Gittin 9:3. Guggenheimer’s English gives Haifa in both passages.
